theorem relPicDeg_relPicMk (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (L : (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic) :
    relPicDeg K (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) L) = classDeg K L :=
  rfl

/-- **E-iv-alg descended to the relative Picard group** (worksheet SB-5, second descent
gadget): the relative degree is invariant under restriction along `Spec` of a `k`-algebra
map `φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂` of field extensions — the degree of a relative Picard class does not
depend on the field over which it is presented. -/
theorem relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap {K₁ K₂ : Type u} [Field K₁] [Algebra k K₁] [Field K₂]
    [Algebra k K₂] (φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂) (x : relPic C (overSpec k K₁)) :
    relPicDeg K₂ (relPicAlgMap C φ x) = relPicDeg K₁ x := by
  induction x using relPic.ind with
  | mk L =>
    have h1 : relPicAlgMap C φ (relPicMk C (overSpec k K₁) L)
        = relPicMk C (overSpec k K₂)
          (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left) L) :=
      relPicMap_mk C (Over.overSpecMap φ) L
    rw [h1, relPicDeg_relPicMk, relPicDeg_relPicMk,
      classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition C φ L]

end AlgebraicGeometry

5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status current with `--status` and its strategy prose current with
60	  `--summary` / `--summary-file` (there is no `--strategy` flag). It doubles as
61	  the **project board**:
62	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
63	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
64	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
65	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
66	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
67	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
68	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
69	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
70	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows

72	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the

74	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
75	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
76	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
77	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
78	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.

80	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread

100	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
101	
102	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
103	
104	| Variable | Meaning |
105	|---|---|
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
112	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |

116	
117	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
118	
119	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
120	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
121	
122	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
123	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
124	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
125	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
126	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
127	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
128	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
129	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
130	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
131	
132	## One-shot discipline (important)
133	
134	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
135	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
136	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
137	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
138	
139	## Pick the highest-value work
140	
141	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
142	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
143	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
144	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
145	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
146	
147	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
148	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
149	the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
150	at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
151	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
152	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
153	(it returns to the queue).
154	
155	## Fresh-context checkpoints
156	
157	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
158	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
159	checkpoints:
160	
161	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
162	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
163	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
164	  clean/build result.
165	
166	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
167	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
168	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
169	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
170	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
171	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
172	terminal `done` claim.
173	
174	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
175	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
176	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
177	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
178	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
179	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
180	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
181	
182	## Warnings are work
183	
184	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
185	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
186	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
187	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
188	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
189	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
190	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
191	why.
192	
193	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
194	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
195	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
196	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
197	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
198	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
199	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
200	
201	## Do the work (Lean)
202	
203	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
204	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
205	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
206	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
207	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
208	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
209	configured final build covers the same files.
210	
211	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
212	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
213	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
214	mathlib — query it:
215	
216	| You want | Use | Not |
217	|---|---|---|
218	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
219	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
220	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
221	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
222	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
223	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
224	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
225	
226	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
227	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
228	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
229	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
230	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
231	back to grep.
232	
233	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
234	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
235	
236	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
237	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
238	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
239	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
240	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
241	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
242	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
243	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
244	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
245	
246	## Read the other projects
247	
248	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
249	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
250	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
251	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
252	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
253	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
254	
255	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
256	
257	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
258	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
259	needs no permission.
260	
261	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
262	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
263	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
264	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
265	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
266	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
267	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
268	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
269	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
270	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
271	
272	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
273	
274	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
275	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
276	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
277	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
278	
279	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
280	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
281	
282	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status (`--status`) and strategy prose
283	  (`--summary`), not a re-narration of the diff.
284	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
285	  as **memory**.
286	
287	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
288	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
289	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
290	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
291	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
292	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
293	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
294	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
295	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
296	
297	## Resuming after an interruption
298	
299	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
300	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
301	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
302	
303	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
304	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
305	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
306	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
307	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
308	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
309	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
310	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
311	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
312	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
313	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
314	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
315	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
316	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
317	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
318	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
319	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
320	
321	## Final report (your last message)
322	
323	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
324	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
325	Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
326	`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and

2	name: project-git
3	description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
4	---
5	
6	Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.
7	
8	## The model
9	
10	- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
11	  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
12	  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
13	  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
14	  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
15	  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
16	  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
17	- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
18	  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
19	  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
20	- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
21	  below). Commit *early and often* with a semantic, math-first message — the
22	  commit message + diff is how your progress is read, so make the message say what
23	  you proved/built. Provenance trailers are added automatically; do not write them.
24	
25	So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
26	Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).
27	
28	## Recording your work (committing)
29	
30	Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
31	`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
32	would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:
33	
34	```bash
35	# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
36	"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
37	"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
38	  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
39	
40	# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
41	git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
42	    add path/to/File.lean
43	git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
44	    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
45	    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
46	```
47	
48	Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
49	files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
50	anything staged in your way.
51	
52	- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
53	  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
54	  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
55	  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
56	  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
57	- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
58	  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
59	  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
60	  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
61	  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
62	  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
63	- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
64	  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
65	- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
66	  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
67	- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
68	  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
69	  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
70	- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
71	  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
72	  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
73	  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
74	  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
75	  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.
76	
77	Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
78	`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
79	make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:
80	
81	```bash
82	"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
83	```
84	
85	## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard
86	
87	Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
88	seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
89	then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
90	plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
91	The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
92	you did not ask for:
93	
94	- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
95	  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
96	  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
97	  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:
98	
99	  ```bash
100	  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
101	  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
102	  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
103	  ```
104	
105	- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
106	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.
107	
108	At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
109	since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
110	blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):
111	
112	```bash
113	"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
114	"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
115	```
116	
117	If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
118	working tree, commit once.
119	
120	## Reading history / a project's diff
121	
122	Run from the workspace root:
123	
124	```bash
125	GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
126	
127	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
128	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
129	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
130	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
131	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
132	```
133	
134	Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
135	`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
136	run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:
137	
138	```bash
139	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
140	  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
141	```
142	
143	To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
144	the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
145	commit changed).
146	
147	## Caveats
148	
149	- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
150	  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
151	  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
152	  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
153	- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

10	# Base-field invariance of the plus-class degree (`w4-datb` §1.2 step 2, the missing brick)
11	
12	`PicEtAff.degAff` reads the degree of a plus class over a field; `PicEtAff.map` restricts a
13	plus class along a base extension of the affine test.  This file proves the one compatibility
14	between them that the tree lacked:
15	
16	  `degAff L (PicEtAff.map C L a) = degAff K a`   for **any** field extension `L/K` over `k`.
17	
18	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegree.lean` records (issue I-0614) that COV-1 / `w4-datb` §1.2 step 2
19	is *not* discharged precisely because this statement is absent — the coverage argument holds the
20	plus-class degree at the fibre field `K` while the presenting Čech class lives over the splitting
21	field `L`, and nothing equated the two readings.  That docstring predicts a lemma "shaped like
22	the landed `degAff_baseFieldShuffle`".
23	
24	## Two corrections to that prediction, both of which make the brick *cheaper*
25	
26	1. **No hypotheses on `L/K`.**  Not finite, not separable, not algebraic.  The prediction's
27	   model (`degAff_baseFieldShuffle`, `Picard/Pic0ThetaAssembly.lean:67`) compares two classes
28	   over one field; here the two *fields* differ, which sounds harder and is not: the
29	   degree of a relative Picard class is invariant along **any** `k`-algebra map of fields
30	   (`relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap`, E-iv-alg descended), so the `L/K` step itself is free.
31	2. **No use of the descent keystone.**  One expects `relPicAlgMap_congr` to reconcile two
32	   different `K`-algebra maps out of the cover carrier.  It is not needed: the two maps are
33	   *literally equal*, by `Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChangeMap_comp_baseChangeInclude`.
34	
35	## The route
36	
37	`degAff` is only *readable* on a finite separable field refinement of the representing cover
38	(`degAff_mk`), so each side needs its own reading field, and the two readings must be compared
39	inside a single field.  That field cannot be chosen freely: for `K = ℚ`, `N = ℚ(i)`, `L = ℝ` no
40	`K`-embedding `N → P` into a finite separable `P/L` exists unless `P` is *built* from `N`.  So:
41	
42	* `N/K` finite separable with `ℓ : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] N` — field cofinality at `K`;
43	* `P/L` finite separable with `q : ((ofField N).baseChange L).Carrier →ₐ[L] P` — field
44	  cofinality applied to the **base-changed field cover**, i.e. `P` is a field factor of
45	  `L ⊗[K] N`.  This is what supplies both `σ : N →ₐ[K] P` and a reading of the `L`-side.
46	
47	Then `j := q ∘ baseChangeMap L ℓ'` reads the `L`-side, and
48	`(j|_K) ∘ E.baseChangeInclude L = σ ∘ ℓ` on the nose, so both sides are `relPicDeg P` of the
49	*same* class and the residual `P`-to-`N` step is E-iv-alg.
50

53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.degAff_map` — **the brick**: `degAff` is invariant under
54	  `PicEtAff.map` along an arbitrary field extension of the test.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.degAff_map_eq_zero_iff` — the degree-zero locus is stable both
56	  ways, the form the coverage argument spends.
57	-/

22	## Why: read what `chartLocus` actually asks for
23	
24	`IsSplitWitness` (`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:151`) — and its own docstring says this at length, under
25	"A convention this predicate INHERITS" — asks for a divisor `W` in the presenting class with
26	`Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))`, and asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  Effectivity and the
27	degree normalisation are what the *chart map's injectivity* needs (GAP-2, `h⁰ = 1`), not what
28	*membership of the locus* needs.
29	
30	The drop (`RiemannRoch/CoverageDrop.lean`) exists to manufacture exactly those two extra
31	properties: it takes a degree-`g+e` witness with `h¹ = 0` and produces an effective `S` with
32	`h⁰(W₀ − S) = 1`.  For membership, that work is thrown away — `mem_chartLocus_of_drop` returns
33	the `IsSplitWitness` half from `hW₀`/`h1` alone, and its own proof shows this: the split witness
34	comes from `isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ m Z M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ h1`, in which the drop,
35	the oracle `P`, `hdense`, `hPcl`, `hPdeg`, `g`, `e`, `hχ` and `hdeg` **do not appear**.
36	
37	So the feedback of step 6 was an artefact of routing coverage through the drop.  Cut the drop
38	and there is one `Z` again — the chart index's — and nothing to feed back.

43	splitting field with vanishing `H¹`.  That is DAT-0a at the fibre field, and it is genuinely

47	(`RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean:71`) produces it, and *derives* the `m` — so what remains of

/-! ## The split witness predicate at a class over a field -/

variable (C) in
/-- **The split witness predicate** (CHART-U(a) in the `w4-datb` §1.6 (a-amendment)
spelling), at a plus class `μ` over a field `K`.

A plus class over a field need not be an honest Čech class — it is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for
an étale cover `E` of `K`.  The amendment's "for some finite separable `L/κ(t)` splitting
the collapsed plus class" is this: there is a finite separable extension `L/K` over which
`μ` becomes `relPicMk` of an honest Čech class `M` on `C_L`, and `M` admits an effective
witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`.

Stated with the witness clause on a *presenting Čech class* rather than on a datum,
because the datum layer is where the shifted-datum constructor (DAT-C GAP-1) is missing;
the two agree through `Pic0ChartLocusClass.mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists`.

## A convention this predicate INHERITS, and which a consumer must not misread

The worksheets say "effective degree-`g` witness with `h¹ = 0`".  The witness clause here —
and the tree's `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing`
(`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:115`) that it mirrors, and the GAP-6 dictionary
`subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (`DivisorFamilyH1Locus.lean:182`) that both rest
on — asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  It asks only for a `CurveDivisor` in the
class with vanishing `H¹`.  That is deliberate on the tree's side: the dictionary is an *iff*
against the engine's complex-form condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗ L)`, and that
condition cannot see effectivity or degree, so adding either clause would break the iff and
with it the openness route.

Two consequences, both load-bearing:

* the degree is supplied **externally**, by the chart-index constraint through
  `degAt_chartTwist` below: on a degree-zero `λ` the twisted class has fibre degree
  `m·d₁ − deg Z`, which the constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − g` makes `+g`.  It is *not* a
  hypothesis of this predicate.  (Until 2026-07-28 this read `−g`, and that sign made the
  locus empty for every `g ≥ 1` — see `degAt_chartTwist` and issue I-0514;
  `chartTwist_chartValue` now pins the direction by the kernel);
* effectivity likewise is not asserted here.  Where the *worksheet's* stronger reading is
  actually needed — the canonical-section normalization `h⁰ = 1`, and GAP-2 uniqueness
  (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`, which does take `0 ≤ D`, `0 ≤ D'`) — the
  effectivity must be re-supplied at that point.  A lane that reads `IsSplitWitness` as
  already giving it will have a gap where it least expects one. -/

      ∧ ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
          Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
            ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule

/-! ## The twisted fibre family -/

variable (C) in
/-- **The twisted family whose chart-membership `chartLocus` tests**: the plus class `λ`
shifted by the Σ-family of `Z` and by `m` inverse powers of the pinned θ-family.

This is the *class-side* half of `chartValue` (`Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`): where
`chartValue` twists the Abel class of a divisor family, `chartTwist` twists an arbitrary
plus class by the same two factors.  A point of `chartLocus` is precisely a point at which
`chartTwist` is realised by an effective divisor with no `H¹` — i.e. at which `λ` itself is
a chart value, after undoing the twist. -/
def chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : picEt C T :=
  lam * (thetaFamily C (thetaCechClass C) T ^ m) * (sigmaFamily C Z T)⁻¹

/-- **The degree ledger of the twist**: at every field point the twisted family has fibre
degree `m·d₁ − deg Z` when `λ` is degree-zero.  With the chart-index constraint
`deg Z = m·d₁ − g` this is `+g`, which is the degree at which an effective witness with
`h¹ = 0` can exist at all.

**Sign discipline, and it was wrong here until 2026-07-28 (issue I-0514).**  `chartTwist`
must be the INVERSE of `chartValue`'s twist, not the same one.  `chartValue` is
`abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹` (`DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`), so recovering the Abel class from a chart
value means multiplying by `θᵐ` and dividing by `Σ` — hence `chartTwist` is
`λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`.  An earlier version applied the `chartValue` twist itself, giving fibre degree
`deg Z − m·d₁ = −g`; since `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))` forces `deg W ≥ g − 1`, that locus was
**empty for every `g ≥ 1`** and its openness was the openness of `∅`.  The comparison point is
`degAt_chartValue` at `n = g` (where the chart index is calibrated and `chartValue` lands in
`pic0`), NOT at `n = 0`.

**An independent confirmation that `+g` is the right target**, worth recording because the
wrong sign survived two sessions: at `deg W = g` the rank anchor
`h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`) gives, for a
witness with `h¹ = 0`,
`h⁰ = deg W + χ(𝒪) = g + (1 − g) = 1` — exactly the `h⁰ = 1` normalization that DAT-C §2 and
GAP-2's uniqueness both require.  So `+g` is not merely the sign that makes the locus nonempty;
it is the unique degree at which the witness is *unique*, which is what the chart map needs to be
injective.  At `−g` the same anchor gives `h⁰ = 1 − 2g`, negative for `g ≥ 1` — the contradiction
that made the locus empty. -/

    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    degAt (chartTwist C m Z T lam) t
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z := by
  rw [chartTwist, degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_mul, degAt_thetaFamily_pow,
    degAt_sigmaFamily, (mem_pic0Subgroup_iff.mp hlam) K t]
  ring

/-- **`chartTwist` inverts `chartValue`'s twist** — the sign check, as a theorem rather than a
docstring claim.

Applying `chartTwist` to a chart value returns the Abel class it came from.  This is the
statement that was FALSE of the earlier definition (which returned
`abelDiv · Σ² · (θᵐ)⁻²`), and it is why the direction is now pinned by the kernel: any future
edit to `chartTwist` that breaks the inversion breaks this lemma.

Recorded per issue I-0514.  A degree ledger alone does not catch a sign error — the wrong-signed
ledger was internally consistent — but an inversion law does. -/
theorem chartTwist_chartValue {n : ℕ} (m : ℕ)
    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
    chartTwist C m Z T (chartValue C π n m Z T s) = abelDiv C π n T s := by
  rw [chartTwist, chartValue]
  group

/-! ## CHART-U(a): the locus -/

variable (C) in
/-- **CHART-U(a), `chartLocus`** (`w4-datc` §3.3, co-signed `w4-datb` §1.6): the set of
points of a general test `T` at which the twisted fibre class `λ_t · θ^m · (−Σ)` has, after
some finite separable splitting of the collapsed plus class at `κ(t)`, an effective witness
divisor with vanishing `H¹`.

The three layers, each supplied by a named brick:
* the *point-to-field-point* passage is `Over.testPoint` (input 0 of this brick — the one

* the *twist* is `chartTwist`, the class-side avatar of `chartValue`;
* the *split witness reading over a field* is `IsSplitWitness`.

This is the RESERVED name of `Pic0ChartLocusClass.lean`'s header, now defined.  Note it is
strictly stronger than `cechWitnessLocus`: general test, twisted class, split predicate. -/
def chartLocus (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) : Set T.left :=
  {t : T.left | IsSplitWitness C
    (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam))}

theorem mem_chartLocus_iff (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left) :
    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam ↔ IsSplitWitness C

/-- **DAT-0a — the P5-uniform `H¹`-vanishing bound.** For a **finite** dominant `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`
compatible with the structure morphisms, there is a single threshold `b : ℤ`, depending only on
`(Y, π)`, past which the degree-one cohomology of `𝒪(D)` vanishes for **every** Weil divisor `D` of
degree `≥ b`:

`∃ b, ∀ D, b ≤ deg D → Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D))`.

The bound is `b = n₁·deg F + 1 − χ(𝒪_Y)`, with `F = fiberWeilDivisor π` and `n₁` the FLV-fiber
threshold at `D₀ = 0`; see the module docstring for the collapsed route
(`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §4 DAT-0a). Consumed by DAT-D's uniform Grassmannian twist. -/
theorem exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1
    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :
    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : Y.CurveDivisor, b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K D →
      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K D) 1) := by
  obtain ⟨n₁, hn₁⟩ :=
    subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ (0 : Y.CurveDivisor)
  have hd'pos : 0 < CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) :=
    zero_lt_deg_fiberWeilDivisor π
  refine ⟨(n₁ : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) + 1
      - Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K), fun D hD => ?_⟩
  -- the residual class `[D] · [F]^{-n₁}`
  set c : Y.CechPic := CurveDivisor.picClass K D
    * (CurveDivisor.picClass K (fiberWeilDivisor π) ^ n₁)⁻¹ with hc
  have hcdeg : classDeg K c
      = CurveDivisor.deg K D - (n₁ : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) := by
    rw [hc, classDeg_mul, classDeg_inv, classDeg_pow, classDeg_picClass, classDeg_picClass]
    ring
  -- an effective witness of the residual class
  obtain ⟨W, hWc⟩ := CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K c
  have hWdeg : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K W + Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) := by
    have hWeq : CurveDivisor.deg K W
        = CurveDivisor.deg K D - (n₁ : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) := by
      rw [← hcdeg, ← hWc, classDeg_picClass]
    linarith
  obtain ⟨E, hEnonneg, hEc⟩ := exists_effective_of_picClass W hWdeg
  -- the witness divisor `n₁ • F + E` is in the class of `D`
  have hclass : CurveDivisor.picClass K (n₁ • fiberWeilDivisor π + E)
      = CurveDivisor.picClass K D := by
    rw [CurveDivisor.picClass_add, picClass_nsmul, hEc, hWc, hc,
      mul_comm (CurveDivisor.picClass K D), ← mul_assoc, mul_inv_cancel, one_mul]
  -- base vanishing at `n₁ • F`, peel `E`, transport along the class
  have hbase : Subsingleton
      (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (n₁ • fiberWeilDivisor π)) 1) := by
    have h := hn₁ n₁ le_rfl
    rwa [zero_add] at h
  have hpeel : Subsingleton
      (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (n₁ • fiberWeilDivisor π + E)) 1) :=

8	/-!
9	# B-5 assembly: from the fibre step to `chartLocus` membership over a GENERAL test
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageFibre.lean` runs `w4-datb` §1.2 steps 4–6 at a splitting field and
12	produces `IsSplitWitness` of a twisted class over `overSpec k L`.  The coverage theorem
13	(§1.2's `pic0_chartLocus_cover`) is a statement about a point `t` of a **general test** `T`:
14	
15	```
16	∃ c : ChartIndex C, t ∈ chartLocus c lam
17	```
18	
19	This file closes the gap between the two, which is one substitution and one collapse:
20	
21	* the fibre class at `t` is `picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam`, a class over the field
22	  `κ(t)` — so the fibre step applies at `K := κ(t)` with no change;
23	* `chartLocus` is *defined* as the split-witness predicate of the twisted class at that field
24	  point, and the twist commutes with restriction (`picEtMap_chartTwist`), so
25	  "`IsSplitWitness` of the twisted fibre class" **is** membership, by `Iff.rfl`.
26	
27	The second point is worth stating as a lemma rather than inlining: `chartTwist` is applied to
28	`lam` over `T` and then restricted, whereas the fibre step produces the twist of the
29	*restricted* class over `κ(t)`.  Those are equal, but not syntactically — `picEtMap_chartTwist`
30	is the law, and `mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre` is the resulting membership rule.
31	
32	## What remains of B-5 after this file
33	
34	**Twice corrected; read the DEFECT section for the full history.**  This header first said the
35	only residues were the two per-fibre choices; a degree probe added a third (step 6's feedback);
36	and on 2026-07-28 that third was **removed again** — not by discharging it but by showing
37	coverage needs no drop, hence no feedback (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`).  Step 2 is
38	likewise landed now (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean`).
39	
40	The two per-fibre choices, which are residues *of the route through this file*:
41	
42	* **step 3, the twist exponent `m`.**  Chosen against the fibre's OWN DAT-0a bound `b_L`.  No
43	  uniform `m₀` exists (§0.2.2, I-0204), so this is a genuine `∃ m` produced inside the
44	  coverage proof, at the fibre.
45	* **step 5's oracle instantiation.**  `Curve/SepPointsDense.lean`'s density keystone at
46	  `P :=` the base-changed `K_s`-points, whose `residueDeg = 1` comes from
47	  `rationalPointBaseChange_snd`.
48	
49	Both are `L`-level statements; neither is `divRep`- or certificate-gated.  Everything between
50	them and `chartLocus` membership is now landed.
51	
52	## Main declarations
53	
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre` — the membership rule: a split
55	  witness for the twisted *fibre* class puts `t` in `chartLocus`.
56	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_drop` — **the B-5 assembly**: the fibre step's
57	  hypotheses, at `K := κ(t)`, give `t ∈ chartLocus`.
58	-/

95	theorem mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre (m : ℕ)
96	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
97	    (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left)
98	    (h : IsSplitWitness C
99	      (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam
100	        * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C m Z) (overSpec k (Over.testPointField t)))) :
101	    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam := by
102	  rw [mem_chartLocus_iff, picEtMap_chartTwist,
103	    chartTwist_eq_mul_thetaFamily_chartTwistClass]
104	  exact h

106	/-! ## A DEFECT IN THIS FILE'S OWN COMPOSITION CLAIM — read before using `mem_chartLocus_of_drop`
107	
108	Found by a degree probe on this file, the same session it was written, and stated here rather
109	than quietly repaired because the theorems below are **true and correctly proved** — what was
110	wrong is the account of how they compose.
111	
112	**The arithmetic.** `hW₀` puts `W₀` in the class `M₀ · (twist class at Z)`.  For a degree-zero
113	`λ` the presenting class `M₀` has `classDeg = 0`, so
114	
115	  `deg W₀ = m·d₁ − deg_k Z`,
116	
117	and `hdeg` demands `deg W₀ = g + e`.  Under the chart-index constraint `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − g`
118	those force **`e = 0`**: the drop budget is zero and the greedy drop does nothing.  (Verified by
119	deriving `(e : ℤ) = 0` from exactly this hypothesis pack.)
120	
121	**What that means.** The pack is *satisfiable* — it instantiates, and at `e = 0` the theorem is
122	the true statement "a witness of degree `g` gives `chartLocus` membership".  It is not vacuous.
123	But `w4-datb` §1.2's argument runs the drop at a **different stage** from the chart index:
124	
125	* the drop runs on `λ·θᵐ` — i.e. at `Z := 0`, where `chartTwistClass C m 0 = θᵐ` and the degree
126	  is `m·d₁`, so the budget is `e = m·d₁ − g`, nonzero for the `m` step 3 chooses;
127	* its **output** `Σ` is then the chart index's `Z`, at which the twisted class has degree `g`.
128	
129	So one `Z` is an input and the other is an output, and this file's headline claim that "steps
130	4–6 are discharged" conflated them.  Steps 4 and 5 (the vanishing witness and the drop) are
131	discharged **at `Z := 0`** by `exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop`; step 6 — feeding `Σ` back as the
132	index and re-reading membership at the *new* `Z` — is **NOT** discharged, and needs the
133	graph-class transport of `Picard/Pic0ChartRationalGraph.lean` applied to the drop's output.
134	
135	**Corrected status of B-5, 2026-07-28 — and the correction is a REMOVAL of both residues this
136	section named.**  The arithmetic above is right and the two-stage reading of `w4-datb` §1.2 is
137	right; what was wrong is treating the drop as *necessary*.
138	
139	* the step-6 feedback is not a residue: coverage needs no drop at all, because
140	  `IsSplitWitness` asks for `h¹ = 0` alone (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`).  With the
141	  drop gone there is one `Z` and nothing to feed back;
142	* step 2 is landed (`PicEtAff.degAff_map` → `classDeg_presenting_eq_zero`).
143	
144	What remains of B-5 is step 3's per-fibre `m`, and even that is now *derived* rather than
145	chosen: `mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` takes the DAT-0a threshold `b_L` in the shape
146	`exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1` produces it, so instantiating DAT-0a at
147	the base-changed curve is the whole remaining work.
148	
149	`mem_chartLocus_of_drop` stays sound and is still the right theorem when the `h⁰ = 1`
150	normalisation is wanted (DAT-C / GAP-2 need it; membership does not); use it knowing its `Z` is
151	the drop's input stage. -/
152	
153	/-! ## The assembly -/
154	
155	variable (C) in
156	/-- **THE B-5 ASSEMBLY** (`w4-datb` §1.2, everything except the two per-fibre choices).
157	
158	For a point `t` of a general test `T` and a plus class `lam` over `T`: given a finite separable
159	`L/κ(t)` presenting the fibre class, and a divisor `W₀` in the twisted class over `L` of degree
160	`g + e` with vanishing `H¹`, the point `t` lies in `chartLocus C m Z lam` — and the drop at `L`
161	additionally yields the `h⁰ = 1` normalisation.
162	
163	**Reading this against `w4-datb` §1.2 — corrected, and the earlier version of this paragraph
164	was wrong in two places** (issues I-0614, I-0615).  It said "steps 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 are all
165	discharged".  Three of those five are; the other two are not:
166	
167	* **step 1 — discharged.**  The `hM₀` hypothesis, which `exists_splitting_of_picEt` supplies
168	  unconditionally.
169	* **step 2 — DISCHARGED 2026-07-28, this line supersedes the "NOT discharged" it replaced.**
170	  The missing input was base-field invariance of `degAff` under `PicEtAff.map`; it is now
171	  `PicEtAff.degAff_map` (`Picard/DegreeZeroBaseField.lean`) and holds for an **arbitrary** field
172	  extension `L/K`, with no finiteness or separability.  Step 2 itself is
173	  `classDeg_presenting_eq_zero` (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean`), and the whole
174	  twisted ledger closes to `g + e` there.
175	* **step 4 — discharged** as an input: `hdeg` + `h1`.
176	* **step 5 — discharged** by the oracle.
177	* **step 6 — NOT NEEDED, which supersedes "NOT discharged".**  The feedback is real for the
178	  route *through the drop*, and the DEFECT section's arithmetic stands.  But coverage does not
179	  need the drop: `IsSplitWitness` asks for `h¹ = 0` and for **neither** effectivity **nor**
180	  degree `g`, so a witness of the twisted class suffices and there is only ever one `Z`.  See
181	  `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`, whose `mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1` strictly
182	  generalises this theorem's membership half — with `g`, `e`, `hχ`, `hdeg` and the whole oracle
183	  deleted rather than discharged.
184	* **step 3 — the residue this paragraph originally named**, and still a residue: `m`, `W₀` and
185	  `hdeg` are *inputs*, because `b_L` is per-fibre and does not transport (I-0204), so no
186	  formulation of this theorem can produce `m` for the caller.
187	
188	**Note one conclusion this theorem deliberately drops and step 6 will want back**: the fibre
189	step returns `S`'s support clause (`coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P`), and the `-` pattern below
190	discards it.  A lane closing step 6 should re-expose it — it is what says `Σ` is supported in
191	the rational points whose graph classes the index is built from. -/
192	theorem mem_chartLocus_of_drop {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left)
193	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
194	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L]
195	    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L]
196	    [Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L] [Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L]
197	    (g e : ℕ) (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
198	    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
199	    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L
200	        (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t) (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam))
201	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
202	    (W₀ : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
203	    (hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀
204	      = M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
205	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (g : ℤ) + e)
206	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1))
207	    (P : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
208	    (hdense : ∀ U : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).Opens,
209	      (U : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
210	    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
211	    (hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L x = 1) :
212	    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam
213	      ∧ ∃ S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧
214	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (e : ℤ) ∧
215	        Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (W₀ - S)) = 1 ∧
216	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
217	          ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (W₀ - S)) 1) := by
218	  obtain ⟨hsplit, S, hS0, hSdeg, -, hSh0, hSh1⟩ :=
219	    exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam) m Z g e hχ M₀ hM₀
220	      W₀ hW₀ hdeg h1 P hdense hPcl hPdeg
221	  exact ⟨mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre C m Z lam t hsplit,

/-!
# `IsChartDatumPresentation`: the FORWARD half, from a pointwise plus-class identity

`IsChartDatumPresentation μ D` (`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:161`) is CHART-U(b)'s one
remaining residue: an `↔`, at every point `t` of an affine test, between

* `D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing κ(t)` — the datum's fibre predicate, and
* `IsSplitWitness C (fibre of μ at κ(t))` — the split predicate `chartLocus` is defined by.

That file's header prices it as a *construction* rather than bookkeeping, and is right to: the
splitting field `L` in `IsSplitWitness` is quantified **per point**, so no single datum obviously
matches it everywhere.

**This file discharges the `→` direction from a hypothesis that mentions no witness at all.**

## What makes the forward direction cheap now

The datum side hands you a witness divisor `W` over `κ(t)` in the class
`CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A κ(t)) D.cechPicClass`, with vanishing `H¹`.  To build
`IsSplitWitness` you must exhibit a finite separable extension over which the *fibre of `μ`* is
honest, with a witness in its class.  Take the extension to be `κ(t)` itself — the identity
extension, finite and separable — and the witness to be `W`.

That is exactly `isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness_self`
(`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistSplit.lean`), the trivial splitting `L := K`.  Memory item I-0564 had
recorded that instance as **unelaborable** and singled it out as "worth wanting"; it is a
one-liner once the existentials are staged rather than bundled, and this file is the first
consumer that needed it.

So the whole forward direction reduces to a statement with **no witness, no `H¹`, no divisor**:
that the datum's fibre class, read as a plus class, *is* the fibre of `μ`.  That is
`IsChartDatumPlusFibre` below — a naturality identity between `PicEtAff.map ∘ picEtAffineEquiv`
and `relPicMk ∘ CechPic.map`, one equation per point.

## What is NOT here, stated so the file is not over-read

The `←` direction.  It is the genuinely harder one and it is where the per-point quantification
of `L` bites: from `IsSplitWitness` you receive *some* extension `L_t/κ(t)`, varying with `t`,
and must produce the datum's predicate at `κ(t)` itself — i.e. descend the witness along
`κ(t) → L_t`.  The tree's fibre-field invariance
(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`) is an `↔` and so does
carry that descent for a *datum* predicate — but the witness one receives lies in `μ`'s class,
not visibly in `D`'s, so closing it still needs the plus-class identity below **plus** the
transport.  Nothing here claims that half.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsChartDatumPlusFibre` — the witness-free hypothesis: the datum presents
  `μ` at every residue field, as plus classes.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitness_of_hasWitnessH1Vanishing` — **the forward half**, pointwise.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_of_converse` — the `↔` assembled from
  the forward half and the one direction still owed, so that a lane closing CHART-U(b) sees
  exactly what is left.
-/

/-!
# C9b: the restricted chart map and the `(f, hf)` pair

`Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` builds the Abel chart map `abelSigmaChart` out of a
representation of the divisor functor, and its header states — correctly — that
`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` is **false as stated for the whole divisor
scheme**: the Abel map has projective spaces `|D|` as fibres, so it is not even a
monomorphism.  It becomes an open immersion only after restriction to the locus where the
fibre is a single point.

This file supplies the restriction, which is the half of C9b that needs no new mathematics
once `chartLocus` exists — and it makes precise which half does.

## What C9b consists of, and which part is here

`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) consumes a pair
`(f, hf)`.  Producing it from `abelSigmaChart` factors into exactly two steps:

1. **restrict the source along an open immersion** — `restrictChart` below.  Given any open
   `V ⊆ D.left`, precomposing `abelSigmaChart` with `yoneda.map V.ι` gives a chart map out of
   `V`, and this is a *composition* of presheaf morphisms.  Landed here, sorry-free.
2. **certify the restricted map an open immersion of presheaves** — the honest content.
   `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` (mathlib `MorphismProperty.relative`) has two clauses:
   relative representability, and the open-immersion property of every represented pullback.
   Step 1 supplies the *left* factor of both clauses for free
   (`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map_of_isOpenImmersion` +
   `MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`), so what remains is exactly the
   corresponding statement for `abelSigmaChart` restricted to `V = chartLocus`, i.e.
   CHART-U(c): on the chart locus the Abel map is a bijection onto its image because the
   normalized effective representative is unique there (DAT-C GAP-2).

So: the *composition* half of the `hf` certificate is discharged here, unconditionally; the
*chart-locus* half is CHART-U(c) and is stated but not proved (it needs GAP-2 plus the
classifier, and the openness of the locus itself, `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`).

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` — an open immersion of schemes is
  an open immersion of presheaves under yoneda.  This is mathlib's `relative_map` at
  `P := IsOpenImmersion`, recorded once with the instances it needs discharged.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.restrictChart` — the chart map restricted to an open of the source.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` — **the composition half of
  `hf`**: if the unrestricted chart map is an open immersion of presheaves, so is any
  restriction of it along an open immersion.  Unconditional in the restriction.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom_restrictChart` — the structure morphism of a restricted chart
  is the restriction of the structure morphism, so the `LocallyOfFiniteType` hypothesis of
  `JacobianData.ofCharts` is inherited (being locally of finite type is local on the
  source).
-/

set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}

/-! ## An open immersion of schemes is one of presheaves -/

/-- **Open immersions transfer through yoneda**: for an open immersion of schemes
`g : X ⟶ Y`, the induced map of yoneda presheaves satisfies `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`.

This is mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative_map` specialised to `F := yoneda` and
`P := @IsOpenImmersion`; the two side conditions it needs — that open immersions are stable
under base change, and that yoneda preserves the relevant pullbacks (it is fully faithful and
`Scheme` has pullbacks) — are discharged by instances.

Recorded as a named lemma because it is the *only* source of `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
facts anywhere in this tree that does not go through a chart certificate: every restriction
of a chart map is built from it. -/
theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsOpenImmersion g] :
    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (yoneda.map g) :=
  MorphismProperty.relative_map (P := @IsOpenImmersion) (F := yoneda) ‹IsOpenImmersion g›

/-! ## The restricted chart map -/

/-- **The chart map restricted to an open of its source.**

`f` is the unrestricted chart map (in practice `abelSigmaChart`, whose source is the divisor
scheme) and `V` an open subscheme of the source; the restriction is the composition with the
yoneda image of the open inclusion.

The point of restricting is that the unrestricted Abel map is *not* an open immersion of
presheaves — see the `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep` header — while its restriction to the locus where
the fibre is a single point is.  This definition is neutral about which open `V` is; the
chart-locus choice enters only in the certificate. -/
def restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (V : X.Opens) : yoneda.obj (V : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
  yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f

/-- **The composition half of the `hf` certificate**: a restriction of an open immersion of
presheaves along an open immersion is again one.

`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is `MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda`, which is stable under
composition (`MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`, needing `yoneda` full and
faithful and `IsOpenImmersion` stable under composition — all instances).  Together with
`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` this discharges, for free and in full generality, the
part of C9b that is bookkeeping.

What it does NOT discharge, and what is therefore the whole remaining content of C9b: the
hypothesis `hfV`.  For `f := abelSigmaChart` that hypothesis is FALSE for `V = ⊤` and is
expected to be true for `V = chartLocus` — it is CHART-U(c), whose proof needs the
uniqueness of the normalized effective representative (DAT-C GAP-2) and the classifier.  A
lane must not read this lemma as reducing C9b to plumbing; it isolates the plumbing so the
mathematics is visible. -/
theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}}
    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (V : X.Opens)
    (hfV : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f) :
    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart f V) :=
  MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderComposition.comp_mem _ _
    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map V.ι) hfV

/-! ## CHART-U(c): the remaining obligation, pinned

With the composition half discharged, `hf` for a restricted Abel chart reduces to a single
statement.  It is pinned here as a definition so that the gate has a name in Lean and not
only in a worksheet — the pattern `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.IsChartDatumPresentation` uses.

**Its field-level input is available.**  DAT-C GAP-2 (Σ-UNIQ-fld) is *landed*:
`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`
(`RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean:144`) — for effective `D`, `D'` with equal Čech class
and `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = 1`, `D' = D`.  (The `w4-datc` §0.3 GAP-2 row claimed no such lemma existed;
that claim was stale and is corrected there as of 2026-07-28.)  What CHART-U(c) still needs
beyond it is the *relative* statement — uniqueness in families over the locus — plus the
classifier `divRepClassifyZar`. -/

variable (C π n) in
/-- **CHART-U(c), pinned**: the chart map is an open immersion of presheaves after restriction
to the locus where the fibre class has a unique effective representative.

This is the whole remaining content of C9b's `hf`.  Stated as a `Prop`-valued definition
rather than proved, because its proof needs the *relative* form of GAP-2 over `chartLocus`
together with `divRepClassifyZar`; a lane that discharges it gets `hf` by feeding it to
`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart`.

Deliberately stated about `abelSigmaChart` and a *given* open `V`, rather than about
`chartLocus` directly: the openness of `chartLocus` is a separate obligation
(`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`), and keeping the two apart means neither has to wait for the
other. -/
def IsChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
    (V : D.left.Opens) : Prop :=
  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V)

/-- The pinned obligation is exactly what `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` would
give from an unrestricted certificate — recorded so that no lane proves the same thing
twice, and so that the *reason* the unrestricted route is unavailable stays visible: the
hypothesis of that lemma is false for the Abel chart at `V = ⊤`. -/
lemma isChartUniv_of_unrestricted {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
